## Full About
Jordan Electric is a family-managed electrical contractor based in Newberry, FL, established in 2026 on more than 20 years of hands-on electrical experience in residential service calls, new construction homes, system upgrades and commercial work. The company holds Florida electrical contractor license EC 13016035, which anyone can confirm on the Florida DBPR public license search (https://www.myfloridalicense.com/wl11.asp). Jordan Electric offers four services: residential electrical services, commercial electrical services, generator installation, and electrical service calls and repairs. Its work is completed to current electrical code.

## Service Details

### Residential Electrical Services
Jordan Electric wires new construction homes, upgrades outdated panels and repairs home electrical systems in Newberry and across Alachua County, completed to current code. A Newberry home needs a residential electrician when it is being built, when its panel can no longer carry what the household runs, or when something stops working the way it should. Jordan Electric handles all three: new construction wiring, panel and system upgrades, and troubleshooting and repairs. Residential service from Jordan Electric covers six kinds of home work: new construction wiring, panel upgrades, system improvements for modern power demands, EV charger installation, troubleshooting and repairs. Every job is completed to current electrical code.

### Commercial Electrical Services
Jordan Electric handles commercial new construction, system upgrades and electrical installations for businesses in Newberry and across Alachua County, planned around your operations. A Newberry business needs a commercial electrician when it builds or fits out a space, when its system cannot keep up with the equipment it runs, or when new installations are needed to grow. Jordan Electric takes on commercial new construction, system upgrades and electrical installations of every size. Send Jordan Electric the address and use of the space, any drawings, what is changing, equipment nameplate ratings, your operating hours and your target date. Those six details let a commercial job be scoped and scheduled around the business from the first conversation.
Page: https://jordan-electric.pageone.cloud/services/commercial-electrical/

### Generator Installation
Jordan Electric installs backup generator systems for homes and businesses in Newberry and across Alachua County, integrated safely with the electrical system already in place. Newberry homes and businesses install backup generators because Florida outages are a matter of when, not if: hurricane season runs June 1 to November 30, and summer thunderstorms drop lines too. A generator tied into the existing electrical system keeps the essentials running until the power returns. Install a generator in the spring, before hurricane season opens on June 1. Activity peaks from mid-August to mid-October, and once a storm is in the forecast there is no longer time to plan, place and connect a system properly. A portable generator is a wheeled unit you start and connect by hand after the power fails; a standby generator sits outside permanently and starts on its own. Either one must feed the house through a proper connection, never through a wall outlet.
Page: https://jordan-electric.pageone.cloud/services/generator-installation/

### Electrical Service Calls & Repairs
Jordan Electric troubleshoots and repairs faulty outlets, lighting problems and system failures at homes and businesses across Alachua County, fixing the source so it stays fixed. Most electrical symptoms point to a loose connection, an overloaded circuit, a failing device or moisture. Heat, burning smells and breakers that will not reset need attention now; flicker and dead outlets can usually wait for a scheduled service call from Jordan Electric. An electrical service call from Jordan Electric covers troubleshooting and repair of faulty outlets and switches, lighting problems and electrical system failures, at homes and at businesses. The aim is to identify the source of the problem and prevent it from recurring.
Page: https://jordan-electric.pageone.cloud/services/electrical-repairs/

## Service Area: Newberry, FL
Electrical work in Newberry is a mix of new-construction wiring for a growing town, careful upgrades inside older downtown buildings, and rural service runs on acreage toward the Gilchrist County line. Jordan Electric plans each job around which of the three it is. In Newberry, the City Building Department issues electrical permits through its SmartGov portal and inspects work against the Florida Building Code and the National Electrical Code. Inspections must be scheduled 24 hours ahead, and the department's phone number is 352-472-3927. Newberry homeowners should know two things: which utility serves the address, and that storms can interrupt power here. Jordan Electric installs backup generator systems for homes and businesses in Newberry, tied into the existing electrical setup so the essentials stay on.

## Frequently Asked Questions

Q: Is Jordan Electric a licensed electrical contractor in Florida?
A: Yes. Jordan Electric holds Florida electrical contractor license EC 13016035. You can confirm any contractor's license on the Florida DBPR license search before you hire, which is a good habit for any electrical work.

Q: What areas does Jordan Electric serve?
A: Jordan Electric is based in Newberry, FL and serves residential and commercial customers across Alachua County and the surrounding areas. Call (352) 472-5511 with your address to confirm we cover it.

Q: Is Jordan Electric a local, family-run company?
A: Yes. Jordan Electric is a family-managed electrical contractor that is locally connected to Alachua County. The company was established in 2026 in Newberry. Read more on the About page.

Q: How long has the Jordan Electric team been doing electrical work?
A: Jordan Electric opened in 2026, and the experience behind it is over 20 years of hands-on electrical work across residential service calls, new construction homes, commercial projects, EV charger installations and generator systems.

Q: Does Jordan Electric work on both homes and businesses?
A: Yes. Jordan Electric handles residential electrical work and commercial electrical work, plus generator installation and service calls for both kinds of property.

Q: Does Jordan Electric wire new construction homes in Newberry?
A: Yes. Jordan Electric wires new construction homes in Newberry and across Alachua County, completed to current electrical code. Talk to us while the plans are still on paper so panel size, circuit layout and space for a generator or EV charger are planned in, not squeezed in later.

Q: Can Jordan Electric upgrade an outdated electrical panel?
A: Yes. Panel and system upgrades are part of Jordan Electric's residential electrical services. Warning signs include breakers that trip when several things run at once, an older or problem-brand panel, or a new 240-volt load such as an EV charger.

Q: Does Jordan Electric install EV chargers?
A: Jordan Electric has hands-on experience with EV charger installations. A Level 2 charger is a 240-volt load, so the panel usually needs a look first. Send the form with your charger model and where you want it, and we will confirm the scope for your home.

Q: Can Jordan Electric install a backup generator for my home or business?
A: Yes. Jordan Electric installs backup generator systems for homes and businesses and integrates each one with the existing electrical setup. The best time to install is before hurricane season starts on June 1. See generator installation for the details.

Q: What does an electrical service call cover?
A: A service call covers troubleshooting and repair of faulty outlets and switches, lighting problems and electrical system failures, at homes and businesses. The aim is to find the source of the problem so it does not come back. See electrical service calls and repairs.

Q: Do you take on commercial electrical projects?
A: Yes. Jordan Electric handles commercial projects of all sizes, including new construction, system upgrades and electrical installations, planned to limit disruption to your daily operations and completed to code. See commercial electrical services.

Q: How much does an electrician cost in Newberry, FL?
A: It depends on the job. The main drivers are the scope of work, the size of the panel or service, the age and accessibility of the existing wiring, whether a permit and inspection are required, and the equipment being installed. A few details about your project let Jordan Electric give you a real figure instead of a guess.

Q: How do I get a quote?
A: Send the contact form or call (352) 472-5511 with the address and what you need. Jordan Electric reviews every request promptly and follows up to schedule. Ask how pricing will work for your specific job when you call.

Q: Can the price change after I get an estimate?
A: It can if the scope changes or if conditions come to light once work begins, such as damaged wiring behind a wall. Only a written agreement fixes the scope and price of a job, so ask for one and ask what would trigger a change before you approve the work.

Q: What happens after I send a request?
A: Jordan Electric reviews the request promptly and follows up to schedule. Include the address, what you need and, for a repair, what you noticed and when it started. The more detail you give, the faster the first conversation goes.

Q: Do electrical repairs or upgrades need a permit in Newberry?
A: Many do. Panel upgrades, service changes and new circuits generally need an electrical permit and inspection, while a like-for-like swap of a fixture or outlet often does not. The building department that covers your address (the City of Newberry inside city limits, Alachua County outside them) sets the rule for your job, so confirm with them or ask when you call.

Q: How do I check that an electrician is licensed in Florida?
A: Use the Florida DBPR license search, look up the contractor by name or license number, and confirm the license is current and for electrical work. Jordan Electric's number is EC 13016035.

Q: How should I prepare for the electrician's visit?
A: Make sure the electrical panel and the work area are clear and reachable, and note what you have seen: which rooms or circuits, when it started and what was running. For a new build or commercial job, have plans or equipment details on hand.

Q: What should I do if I smell burning or see sparks?
A: If you see smoke or flame, leave the building and call 911. For a hot outlet or burning smell, switch off that circuit at the panel only if you can do it safely, stop using it and call. Never open a panel cover or touch a scorched device. The repairs page has a symptom guide.
